findings.title: Clone the shutdown handle before creating the native controller
findings.impact: If the newly added UnixStream clone fails, for example because the native process has exhausted its file descriptors, registration exits after the daemon has created the attachment controller but before a NativeControl exists. The only returned controller capability is discarded, while the daemon retains that disconnected registration. Repeated failed attachment attempts can consume the 4096-controller limit and eventually prevent otherwise valid attachments.
findings.evidence: NativeControl::register receives controller-create successfully at lines175-178, then propagates connection.shutdown_handle() failure at line179. client::Connection::shutdown_handle delegates to UnixStream::try_clone, which is fallible. NativeControl::stop/Drop cannot run because Self has not been constructed. On socket departure, daemon::serve invokes Registry::depart; src/control.rs:855-872 only marks the view disconnected and does not remove its controller. Removal requires an explicit guarded close in src/control.rs:1052-1085. The fallible clone after controller creation is added by this patch.
findings.fix: Move connection.shutdown_handle()? before the controller-create RPC, so this local allocation failure cannot leave a newly minted daemon registration behind. Alternatively, explicitly close the still-unowned newly created controller before propagating that error; do not release ownership or cancel claims as cleanup.
